correctness.rationale: All edge-local Gram integrals and sign roots are exact; the nodal block H=(3D-A)/24 has a strictly positive Neumann-series inverse and sum d_v a_v=12; vertex kernels give the sharp 79/25 upper ceiling with strict cancellation. Orthogonal bubble decomposition gives an explicit interior envelope strictly below 79/25. On hypercubes, a Hamming shell-moment estimate bounds cancellation by 158/(25d) and proves the limiting optimum. The positivity defect follows from P1=1 and the negative-part kernel identity. The standalone exact-rational program independently reconstructs local and global kernels from two bases. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: A natural global approximation operator is sharply controlled over all finite branched metric graphs with arbitrary positive edge weights. The explicit constant 79/25 is optimal but unattained, witnessed by degree-growing hypercubes; this structural result is not a routine numerical recomputation or a special graph substitution. A sharp nontrivial positivity-loss constant 27/25 follows from the same kernel geometry. It distinguishes graph-dimensional branching from known 2D simplicial instability and strengthens earlier quadratic computations restricted to quadratic stars and cliques.
